messages.subject: Intercept-only model
parts:
Hi all,

Apologies if this has already been asked - a quick search through the forum didn't turn up anything.  

I'm getting the following error when I fit an intercept-only model and am wondering if it's because my model syntax is bogus, or there's an issue with some package version (matrix package maybe)?  

Error: non-conformable matrix dimensions in .diag2T.smart(e1, e2, kind = "d") - e2

Here is code to reproduce the error:

library(INLA)
library(inlabru)

# Simulate data
dat <- data.frame(y = rbinom(100,1,0.1))

# Analysis
comps <- ~ Intercept(1)

present_like <- like(
  family = "binomial",
  data = dat,
  formula = as.formula('y ~ Intercept')
)

fit <- bru(
  comps,
  present_like,
  options = list(bru_verbose = 4,
                 bru_debug = TRUE)
)

Note that if I add an additional covariate effect, the model will fit without an error:

library(INLA)
library(inlabru)

# Simulate data
dat <- data.frame(y = rbinom(100,1,0.1),
                  x = rnorm(100))

# Analysis
comps <- ~ Intercept(1) + x_effect(x)

present_like <- like(
  family = "binomial",
  data = dat,
  formula = y ~ Intercept + x_effect
)

fit <- bru(
  comps,
  present_like,
  options = list(bru_verbose = 4)
)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Intercept-only model
parts:
For intercept-only models, bru() needs a bit of help to understand how large the predictor vector is supposed to be (due to the internal software architecture, it can’t currently easily understand that from the response variable, but may in the future.

Use
  + Intercept(rep(1, NROW(.data.)))
to assist it.

Finn
